title: SpaceX conducts 13th Starship test flight
summary: SpaceX successfully conducted the 13th suborbital test flight of its Starship rocket on July 24, addressing issues from the previous flight and deploying functioning satellites for the first time.

title: ULA deals with financial challenges caused by Vulcan grounding
summary: United Launch Alliance (ULA) has secured a loan from its corporate parents to address financial challenges stemming from the grounding of its Vulcan Centaur rocket. The company is navigating these difficulties as it awaits the rocket's return to flight.

title: LatConnect 60 Unveils Proprietary AI Capabilities Following Growing Indo-Pacific Defence Interest in SWIRSAT
summary: LatConnect 60 introduced proprietary AI capabilities for its Earth observation satellites, responding to increased defense interest in the Indo-Pacific region, particularly for SWIRSAT.

title: Office of Space Commerce to move ahead on mission authorization
summary: The Commerce Department is advancing plans for a voluntary mission authorization system to regulate novel space activities not covered by existing agencies. This initiative aims to fill regulatory gaps for emerging space missions.

title: Lightning strikes Long March 3B after liftoff, Kinetica-1 launches 5 satellites
summary: A Long March 3B rocket successfully delivered its payload to orbit despite being struck by lightning shortly after liftoff. Separately, Kinetica-1 launched five satellites.
company: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC)

title: EU delays release of Copernicus imagery over Gulf of Oman
summary: The European Union delayed the release of certain Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery for 24 hours after a U.S. request, citing concerns over the Gulf of Oman region.

title: Air Force takes over troubled military GPS receiver program
summary: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center will now oversee the development, integration, and sustainment of military GPS receiver equipment. This move aims to address issues with the program accessing the military’s encrypted GPS signal.
company: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center

title: NASA programs feel effects of workforce reductions
summary: NASA reports that over two dozen major projects have been impacted by a 20% reduction in its civil servant workforce over the past year. The workforce cuts are affecting critical programs across the agency.

title: Poland commits $745 million to EU’s IRIS² constellation project
summary: Poland has committed $745 million to the EU's IRIS² satellite internet constellation project. The investment aims to support the development of a multi-orbit satellite internet system.

title: Mark Matossian co-founds Whipsmart Ventures to fund space and deep tech
summary: Mark Matossian, a space startup veteran, co-founded Whipsmart Ventures, a venture capital fund specializing in space and deep tech. The fund is backed by a software engineer and a best-selling author.

title: We talk with astronaut Michael Foale about the 1997 Space Station Mir crisis: 'He took all the blame of the collision on his shoulders'
summary: Astronaut Michael Foale reflects on the 1997 Space Station Mir collision crisis, stating he took full responsibility for the incident. He credits the crew with saving the station during the emergency.

title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 220 — First on Mars
summary: The 220th episode of the 'This Week In Space' podcast discusses the 50th anniversary of Viking 1's Mars landing, featuring guests Dr. Pascal Lee and Dr. Penny Boston.

title: An off-the-shelf camera could help us find more black holes smashing together
summary: A readily available off-the-shelf camera could enhance the detection of black hole collisions without requiring new technology, addressing a long-standing instrumentation challenge for LIGO.

title: NASA astronaut, 2 cosmonauts returning to Earth on July 26: Watch it live
summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Russian cosmonauts will return to Earth from the International Space Station on July 26. Their homecoming can be watched live.

title: SpaceX's Starship megarocket makes the 'softest splashdown' ever after launching next-gen Starlink satellites in Flight 13 test (video)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched its Starship megarocket on its 13th test flight, deploying next-gen Starlink satellites and achieving the 'softest splashdown' ever. The mission marked a significant milestone with a surprising successful conclusion.

title: ZWO Seestar S30 Pro smart telescope review
summary: The ZWO Seestar S30 Pro is a compact, automated smart telescope featuring a higher resolution upgrade. This review highlights its advanced capabilities and compact design.

title: We boldly chat with 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' showrunners about space dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors for season 4 (interview)
summary: The showrunners of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' discuss plans for season 4, including the introduction of space dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors. They express excitement about incorporating these elements into the show.

title: What lurks beneath the volcanoes of Jupiter's moon Io? NASA's Juno probe just took a peek
summary: NASA's Juno probe has provided new insights into the subsurface of Jupiter's moon Io by studying its volcanoes. These findings could revolutionize the understanding of volcanic activity across the solar system, including Earth.

title: Planet hunter gets the silent treatment | Space photo of the day for July 24, 2026
summary: ESA's Plato spacecraft has completed critical testing ahead of its upcoming spaceflight. The mission aims to hunt for exoplanets as part of the agency's planet-hunting efforts.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the rocket for its upcoming missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX during its third attempt. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's Starship development program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully arrived at the International Space Station (ISS), expanding the station's crew by three members. A U.S. extravehicular activity (EVA) was conducted to complete repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay highlights ongoing technical challenges in the Starship program.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman from Florida. The Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV-1) aims to demonstrate in-space servicing capabilities.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9, Starship, and Chinese rockets scheduled to launch
summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new launch attempt of Starship Flight 13 after a previous abort. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are scheduled for upcoming launches.

title: Making Progress: Relativity’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and PLD Space’s Miura 5
summary: Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space are making progress on their respective launch vehicles: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5. While Starship's test program has dominated recent attention, these companies continue advancing their medium-to-heavy lift rocket developments.

title: China’s first recovered booster returns to port as LandSpace aims for first land recovery
summary: China achieved a milestone with the first successful recovery of a booster, and LandSpace is now aiming for its first land recovery.

title: Soyuz MS-29 launches new crew to ISS from Baikonur
summary: Soyuz MS-29 successfully launched a new crew to the International Space Station (ISS) from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on July 14. This marks another crewed mission to the orbiting laboratory.

title: Launch Preview: Soyuz to launch crew to ISS, Starship to fly another test flight
summary: Soyuz is set to launch a crew to the International Space Station (ISS), while SpaceX's Starship is preparing for its 13th flight test. Seven launches are scheduled globally this week.

title: TEC Business to Business website
summary: The TEC Business to Business website reported on an unspecified space industry news. No specific details about the content or event were provided.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary by releasing a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over the past five decades. The publication underscores the agency's significant contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: Next-generation antennas are being enhanced by advanced silicon-based technologies. These innovations are poised to revolutionize communication and sensing capabilities in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: The European Space Agency's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in ESTEC's Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are ready for space. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting industry events to present follow-up actions from the CM25 ministerial meeting held in November 2025. These events aim to inform industry about planned activities, priorities, and opportunities within ESA programs.

title: One robotic arm to rule them all
summary: The article discusses a groundbreaking robotic arm technology that aims to revolutionize space operations. This innovation is expected to enhance efficiency and capabilities in satellite servicing and space station maintenance.

title: We’re back: Proba-3 ready for more science
summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and ASPIICS instrument are fully operational and ready to resume formation flying to create artificial eclipses. This marks the resumption of routine science operations for the mission.

title: ESA’s Prodex programme brings scientific research to space
summary: ESA's Prodex programme has enabled the successful launch of the 4DSpace-Daedalus mission in Norway. The programme supports research institutes in participating in European space science activities and missions.

title: ESA Puts €65M Behind Europe’s First Lunar Ice Rover
summary: ESA has committed €65 million to Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. This marks a significant step for Europe's involvement in lunar exploration.

title: Lunar Outpost Plans to Fly NVIDIA Chips to the Moon
summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA chips to the Moon, merging the semiconductor and space exploration industries. This initiative highlights the growing intersection of technology and lunar missions.

title: A Deep Dive into the Bluetooth Satellite Connectivity Market Following the FCC’s Proposal
summary: The FCC is proposing to open unlicensed Bluetooth and Wi-Fi frequencies for space-based communications. This move could significantly impact the Bluetooth satellite connectivity market.

title: FCC Filings Show Eutelsat is Working on a New 528-sat Constellation Beyond OneWeb
summary: FCC filings indicate Eutelsat is developing a new constellation of 528 satellites, separate from its OneWeb program. The company suggests that the Next program is not yet fully developed.

title: NASA Puts $2B Price Tag on Nuclear Mars Mission
summary: NASA has estimated a $2 billion cost for the Space Reactor-1 Freedom, a fission-powered spacecraft designed for interplanetary missions to Mars. This marks the first such initiative to develop a nuclear-powered spacecraft for deep space exploration.

title: Intel Authorization Act Proposes Limiting Commercial EO Access
summary: The Intel Authorization Act seeks to restrict commercial Earth observation (EO) satellite operators from sharing data with the public. The U.S. government argues that EO data is a privilege, not a right, and aims to control its dissemination.

title: The UK Scraps the Department in Charge of UKSA
summary: The UK has decided to abolish the department overseeing the UK Space Agency (UKSA) during the Farnborough Air Show. This move was announced by the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

title: The UK and Space Florida Launch Joint Fund
summary: The UK and Space Florida have launched a joint fund to support projects with partners from both regions. This initiative aims to foster collaboration between the UK and Florida's space sectors.

title: Breaking Down the $686B Space Economy
summary: The global space economy reached a record $686 billion in 2025, as reported by the Space Foundation. This marks significant growth in the industry's economic impact.

title: FCC Eyes Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Bands for Satellites
summary: The FCC is considering a proposal to permit unlicensed wireless devices like Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to communicate directly with satellites. This move aims to expand satellite connectivity for consumer devices.

title: NASA to Support New Glenn Hot Fire Testing at Stennis Space Center
summary: NASA and Blue Origin will collaborate on second stage hot fire testing for the New Glenn rocket at NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. This partnership aims to advance the development of the New Glenn rocket.

title: Two Galileo Satellites Enter Service for Europe
summary: Two new Galileo satellites, SAT 33 and SAT 34, have entered service, enhancing Europe's satellite navigation system. The European Space Agency (ESA) announced their operational status, boosting the Galileo constellation's capabilities.

title: Telco CEOs Shut Down the Idea of Satellite MVNO, Say LEO Isn’t a Threat to Broadband
summary: Top telco CEOs dismissed the idea of forming a satellite MVNO agreement, stating that LEO satellite broadband is not a significant threat to their broadband services.

title: Space Is Coming for Silicon
summary: SpaceX has introduced Starmind, an AI satellite megaconstellation developed by Elon Musk. This marks a significant step in the development of branded orbital data centers in space.

title: Iceye and KT SAT Partner on Flood Intelligence in South Korea
summary: Iceye and KT SAT have formed a strategic partnership to provide flood monitoring solutions in South Korea for government and commercial entities. This collaboration represents the first deployment of Iceye's solutions in the country.

title: Intellian Releases New Terminal for Iridium GMDSS Service
summary: Intellian has launched a new terminal for Iridium's GMDSS maritime safety service, utilizing the Iridium Certus 100 service. The terminal was announced on Thursday.

title: Frequency Electronics Reports Increased Demand From Proliferated Satellite Programs
summary: Frequency Electronics reported $18 million in recent contract wins, including an $11 million award from an undisclosed major aerospace prime contractor for a proliferated satellite program.

title: FCC Approves a New C-Band Auction
summary: The FCC approved a new C-band auction to clear 160 megahertz of the upper C-band spectrum, aiming to build on previous auctions. This move is expected to benefit satellite operators and the broader wireless industry.

title: Lite Coms Wins $22M Contract to Support Operational Readiness
summary: Lite Coms secured a $22 million contract from an unnamed government and defense customer to provide satellite communications for operational readiness. The company specializes in integration and manufacturing of satellite communication solutions.

title: FCC Overhauls Satellite Licensing, Adopts ‘Assembly Line’ Approach
summary: The FCC approved a major overhaul of its satellite licensing process, introducing a streamlined 'licensing assembly line' approach to expedite approvals. The new system aims to modernize and accelerate the licensing of space and earth station operations.
